We’re introducing new ways to create and refine files and code in the Gemini app. You can now generate, preview, and edit files right within your Gemini app chat—expand to full screen to type edits directly, highlight text to ask questions, or have Gemini refine them. PDF preview and editing is supported on both the web and mobile, while all other formats (documents, spreadsheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code) are supported on the web only. Here are just some of the new things you can do:


Generate and refine slide decks: Create presentation outlines or slide content, preview the layout in chat, and edit directly or ask Gemini to adjust the tone and structure before opening in Google Slides, or downloading as a PPTX or PDF.
Build and export Google Sheets: Generate structured trackers, tables, and data models from a prompt, preview them in Gemini, and open them directly in Google Sheets.
Edit documents and PDFs: Quickly draft PDFs, Google Docs, LaTeX, Markdown, or TXT files, and make manual or prompted edits inline on web or in a full-screen view—plus you can upload all of them to Drive.


These capabilities are now available to all users in all languages where the Gemini app is available.

# Gemini Can Now Create and Edit Files in Chat: What It Does and Who It's For

> **In short:** Google says the Gemini app can now generate, preview, and edit files inside the chat itself. PDFs work on the web and on mobile, while documents, spreadsheets, slide decks, and code are web-only. Edited files can go to Google Drive, Google Slides, or Google Sheets.

Think about the last time you needed a simple checklist, a short report, or a tidy table. You probably opened a document app, made a blank file, and started typing from scratch. Google's update aims to shorten that process by letting you build the file in the same conversation where you asked for it.

## What's new

Google says you can now create and refine files and code right inside the Gemini app chat. Here are the three main things it highlights:

- **Slide decks:** Ask for a presentation outline or slide content, look at the layout in the chat, and ask Gemini to adjust the tone or structure. When you're happy, you can open it in Google Slides or download it as a PPTX (the standard PowerPoint file format) or a PDF.
- **Spreadsheets:** Ask for a tracker, a table, or a simple data model. You can preview it in Gemini and open it directly in Google Sheets.
- **Documents and PDFs:** Gemini can draft PDFs (portable documents that look the same on any device), Google Docs, LaTeX (a formatting language often used for scientific papers), Markdown (plain text with simple formatting marks), and TXT (plain text) files. You can edit them in the chat or in a full-screen view.

## How the editing works

The part that makes this more than a generator is editing. Google describes a few ways to change a file:

- **Type your own edits** after expanding the file to full screen.
- **Highlight a piece of text** and ask Gemini a question about it.
- **Ask Gemini to refine it**, for example by changing the tone or reorganizing the sections.

Google also says you can upload these files to Drive, its cloud storage service, so they're saved alongside your other documents.

## Where it works

PDF preview and editing work on both the web and mobile. Documents, spreadsheets, slide decks, Markdown, TXT, and code are web-only for now. Google says the features are available to all users, in every language where the Gemini app is offered. Users of all ages who have access to the app can generate files. Admins have no separate control over this feature.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** If you plan a trip, a budget, or a study schedule, ask for a table or a checklist and fix the details in the same chat.
- **For your business or work:** Draft an outline for a slide deck or a one-page summary, then polish it in Google Slides or Docs.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with a simple request, such as a grocery list as a TXT file or a one-page PDF. Small files make it easy to see how the edits work.
- **If you already use it:** Try highlighting one paragraph and asking Gemini to rewrite only that section, then compare the result with the full-screen edits you make by hand.

## Wrap-up

Google's update lets you make and fix everyday files inside Gemini instead of switching between several apps. The features are simple to explain: generate, preview, and edit in the chat, then move the finished file to Drive, Slides, or Sheets. Your next step is easy: open the Gemini app today and ask it for a small file, such as a checklist or a short table. Then try one edit, either by typing it yourself or by highlighting text and asking for a change.
